newsitem.title: USA: Appeal filed in AMR expansion at Miami.
newsitem.headline: Appeal filed in AMR expansion at Miami.

text.p: Six airlines have appealed a federal ruling that the funding formula was fair for AMR Corp's new $1 billion terminal at Miami International Airport, the plaintiffs' lawyer said Wednesday.
The appeal was filed April 18 in the U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia, plaintiffs' attorney Barry Davidson said. No hearing has been scheduled.
In March the U.S. Department of Transportation approved Dade County's method for calculating rates and charges, clearing the way for terminal construction.
Dade County operates the Miami airport and plans to issue revenue bonds to build the new terminal for AMR's American Airlines.
The competing carriers alleged that they were being asked to pay higher airport fees to subsidize facilities that would be used only by American.
The plaintffs are UAL Corp's United Airlines, Delta Air Lines Inc, US Airways Group Inc, Trans World Airlines Inc, Air Canada and Deutsche Lufthansa AG.
The appeal said the DOT ruling ignored an administrative law judge's finding that the rate structure was unfair, and that it applied the wrong standard in its rate review, Davidson said.

In Miami Tuesday, AMR chief executive Robert Crandall said the company was ready to move ahead with the 47-gate terminal. He said it would be the focal point of the airline's plan to create a "major connecting hub" to Europe and Latin America.
AMR's American and American Eagle commuter operation currently have 300 flights a day at Miami International, accounting for more than half of the flights through the airport.
